summary.headline: Seshaasai Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.6% YoY to INR 405 crore with EBITDA margin of 30.8%; FY26 revenue fell 1.5% to INR 1,441 crore, no FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR 404-405 crore, up 8.1% QoQ and 9.6% YoY, led by communication and fulfilment and IoT. EBITDA was about INR 125 crore (30.8% margin, up 330 bps YoY) and PAT about INR 82 crore (20.2% margin, up 316 bps YoY), helped by lower finance costs after IPO debt repayment and interest income on IPO funds. For FY26, revenue declined 1.5% to INR 1,441 crore on a temporary moderation in Payment Solutions, while EBITDA reached INR 394 crore (27.4% margin) and PAT INR 240 crore (16.7% margin). Management declined to give FY27 guidance, deferring any update until after Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 398 crore, incl. ~INR 195 crore unutilised IPO funds

segments.name: Payment Solutions
segments.commentary: About 47.5% of Q4 revenue and ~50% of FY26 revenue; hit by PSU/private bank issuance moderation and low COVID-era renewal base. Added 21 new bank/fintech customers, lost none; won a multi-year PSU bank tender worth ~INR 8.7 crore. Metal cards are ~4% of the segment.

segments.name: Communication and Fulfilment Solutions
segments.commentary: 39% of FY26 revenue (39.8% of Q4) and grew 29% YoY; added ~8 customers. Management expects a marginal decline in FY27 but described the segment as stable.

segments.name: IoT Solutions
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue (12.4% of Q4), grew about 45-48% YoY (figures varied across the call). Added ~65 customers. RFID utilisation about 70% for FY26 and 80-85% in Q4. SIM division began material revenue in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue guidance by segment; management will revisit after Q1 FY27 given geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
No margin guidance for FY27/FY28; management expects product mix shift to IoT, eSIM and other solutions to support good margins.
IoT revenue expected to grow faster than the ~47% achieved in FY26.
eSIM commercial revenue expected from H2 FY27, after a compliance step due July/August 2026.
Capex of about INR 160-200 crore through FY27 across Payment Solutions and IoT, plus modernisation, partly funded from IPO proceeds.
Payment card business expected to bottom out, with renewal volumes to recover.
capex_capacity: Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities became operational in Q4 FY26; Nagpur and Bengaluru still under construction.
SIM capacity about 7 million per month, running at about 30% utilisation.
eSIM capacity of 2-3 million per month depending on form factor; commercial production not yet started.
RFID capacity utilisation about 70% for FY26 and 80-85% in Q4 FY26; three plants can do inlay manufacturing.
Bengaluru facility received GSMA SAS-UP certification for SIM/eSIM manufacturing and personalisation.
demand_pricing: Payment card demand weakened due to lower issuance from PSU and private banks, COVID-era renewal base effects, and tighter bank and fintech compliance.
Top 10 customers contributed about 62.8% of FY26 revenue; 96.6% of revenue came from existing customers.
Gross margin improved on 7-8% material cost savings from procurement consolidation and inventory planning; management said FX was an adverse factor in Q4.
Export revenue about INR 3 crore in FY26; international work is via partners, with some overseas fintech RFPs at evaluation stage.
Domestic payment scheme and global fintech RFPs for metal card variants still under evaluation.
Market share of payment cards in India was 31.6% in FY25 per industry analysts.

qa_highlights.question: Will rupee depreciation hurt gross margins going into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin gains came from sourcing savings of 7-8% on top raw material categories plus operating leverage. Q4 FX was adverse but mostly hit materials bought earlier, so the exposure is still to be watched.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital intensity rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built up to manage global supply risks in Q1 and Q4, and surplus IPO cash inflates the cash line. Receivables and inventory are said to be in line with the business, with monitoring under way.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 guidance by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management will wait until Q1 FY27 for better visibility on the macro and geopolitical situation before guiding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the eSIM timeline and SIM capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: SIM is at about 30% utilisation of 7 million per month capacity and already supplies a leading telecom player. eSIM commercial production is expected after a July/August compliance step, with revenue from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the payment card business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the business to bottom out, with renewal volumes recovering from the COVID-era base and growth from premiumisation, transit and state-government card programmes; metal cards were about 4% of the segment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for backward integration into chips or inlays?
qa_highlights.answer: Inlay equipment has been in place for about 2.5 years and three plants can make inlays. Management said local inlay making will improve margins once it reaches scale, but gave no margin quantification and parked chip integration for now.

risks_watch: Payment Solutions volume recovery depends on bank renewal cycles and regulatory conditions; the segment is about half of revenue.
Rupee depreciation, input cost inflation and supply-chain constraints could pressure gross margins; management said input prices are rising.
eSIM commercial launch depends on the July/August compliance step and integration work; SIM utilisation is only about 30%.
Working capital days have risen over two years; inventory and receivables are being monitored.
Top 10 customers are 62.8% of revenue, so concentration risk remains.
Unutilised IPO proceeds of about INR 195 crore are to be deployed in later periods.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on operations and margins but noticeably reticent on forward numbers: management declined FY27 segment, margin and eSIM revenue guidance, citing geopolitical and macro uncertainty. Confidence is strongest on IoT, metal cards and the margin trajectory.
key_quotes: We believe FY '26 should be viewed not only as a year of resilience during a softer industry phase but also as a validation of our diversified and relationship -led business model.
Pavan, at this point in time, it's difficult to give guidance for FY '27, considering the macroeconomic environment, etc.
we would like to probably wait until Q1, where we get a better grip of the situation, better visibility, and maybe in a position to give a guidance after Q1.
